title: Backwards‑Tolerant OpenAI ChatCompletions Mapping and Streaming Reconciliation
creator: Nina Patel
description: Implement a backwards‑tolerant compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response shapes to Redwood's canonical streaming and function‑call model. Objective: allow legacy clients to interact with Redwood runtime without changing client code while preserving structured output and high‑fidelity streaming semantics. Scope includes request shape normalizers, response rewriters, partial chunk reassembly, function_call preservation, metadata provenance, and error-code equivalence mapping. This ticket focuses on the runtime side mapping + automated integration tests; follow‑ups will cover Console telemetry and Dedicated rollout knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy OpenAI request payloads (messages array, max_tokens, stop, presence_penalty) are accepted and mapped to Redwood API internal request model without loss of intent.
Streaming SSE/chunked responses emitted to legacy clients conform to OpenAI framing (delta events) while preserving structured 'function_call' sequences and final aggregated JSON output.
Partial stream reconnection: client reconnect within 30s is resumed with idempotent reassembly and no duplicate tool invocations in 95% of test scenarios.

Tool/function call side‑effects are executed exactly once across retries by leveraging request fingerprinting and idempotency keys, and legacy 'finish_reason' values are translated to Redwood outcome reasons.
Latency regression vs. current proxy baseline < 15% at p95 under standard perf harness; unit and integration test coverage >= 85% for mapping code paths.
implementation_notes: Accept both 'role' strings and 'author' legacy alias; normalize to internal role enum at ingress.
Map OpenAI 'function_call' blocks to Redwood tool invocation envelope; persist original function.name in provenance metadata header 'x-oa-fnname'.
For streaming, translate incremental 'delta' tokens into Redwood framed events while emitting 'function_call' partial payloads as separate events to avoid blocking streaming of textual deltas.
Introduce a lightweight request fingerprint computed from user_id + normalized_messages_hash + client_timestamp to drive idempotency for tool calls (stored in Redis with TTL).
Support legacy 'stop' arrays by converting into Redwood termination predicates and preserve ordering semantics for multi‑stop tokens.
Error mapping: convert Redwood internal errors to OpenAI compatible codes (e.g., RedwoodQuotaExceeded -> 429 with 'rate_limit' hint).
Edge cases: handle clients sending both 'messages' and 'prompt' — prefer 'messages' but record ambiguity to logs and raise a non-blocking telemetry event.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Streaming order divergence may cause function_call payloads to arrive after downstream tool execution starts. Mitigation: buffer function_call finalization until function payload fully received or 500ms max window expires.
Risk: Idempotency keys collide for active multi‑tenant workloads. Mitigation: namespace keys by tenant_id and include sequence nonce when high concurrency detected.
Risk: Legacy clients expect strict OpenAI finish_reason strings. Mitigation: produce canonical mapping table and a compatibility header 'x-rw-oa-reason' for debugging.
Risk: Increased CPU overhead for realtime reassembly. Mitigation: offload heavy parsing to worker pool and use sampled tracing for hot paths.
work_log: 2026-02-18: Ticket created by Nina with initial scope and acceptance criteria.

2026-02-20: Spike completed by Carlos — validated that existing streaming runtime can emit custom framed events without breaking existing clients. Spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/spikes/openai-compat-streaming (internal).
2026-02-24: Design review with PM and infra. Decision: use Redis for short‑lived idempotency locks; persist function_call provenance in audit log stream.
2026-02-28: Implemented request normalizer prototype in rw-compat package; created branch github.com/redwood-inference/rw-compat/compare/ENG-318271-normalizer.

2026-03-04: Integration test harness added — replayed 500 legacy session traces from prod-samples; 12 failures discovered (mostly finish_reason mapping), created followup ENG-318272 for finish_reason canonicalization.
2026-03-08: PR submitted for streaming shim: PR #2324. CI: unit tests passing, flakey SSE test failing intermittently. Triggered ticket ENG-318274 for flaky test investigation.
2026-03-10: Mid-sprint sync: replacing Redis key implementation with tenant namespacing; performance benchmark planned for 2026-03-12.
qa_plan: Unit tests for each normalizer path (role aliases, prompt + messages ambiguity, stop conversions).
Integration tests: end‑to‑end flow from legacy client emulator -> compatibility layer -> runtime -> tool backend; assert single tool invocation and correct final output.
Chaos test: simulate network interruptions during streaming and assert idempotent reassembly and no duplicated tool calls in 500 randomized seeds.
Perf test: run 10k requests synthetic workload comparing baseline proxy vs new mapping layer; capture p50/p95 latency and CPU.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: behind feature flag in staging for 100% of internal dev tenants.
Phase 2: Canary for 5% of legacy‑tagged production traffic with strict telemetry collection.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with automatic fallback to legacy proxy on error rate > 1% or p95 latency regression > 20%.
Phase 4: Full switch and deprecation notice to legacy proxy, keep compatibility layer in maintenance mode.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on idempotency algorithm and Redis namespace edge cases.
Verify that function_call partial streaming events do not leak sensitive argument contents — ensure argument redaction rules are applied prior to emission.
Check the finish_reason mapping table in the design spec for completeness against the latest OpenAI docs.
